subject: Erase-trigger and retention tier options — DPA redline questions
messages:
From: Samira Qureshi <samira.qureshi@aurumhealth.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@aurumhealth.io
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Erase-trigger and retention tier questions (DPA redline)

Hi Rishi / Marissa —

Thanks for taking the time on the DPA redlines. We've reviewed Redwood's proposed language and have a few specific questions around the retention/erasure and backup carve-outs before we can sign off:

1) Backups: the redline currently allows for encrypted backups to be retained for "business continuity" without a firm max. Our security team needs explicit bounds. Can you confirm maximum retention for immutable backups and whether backups are ever stored outside the EU?

2) Certified erasure: your clause references a 90-day erase window and a certification process. Does certification include destruction of any onshore fallbacks or copies? What is the evidence you can supply?

3) Legal hold / lawful access: if Aurum is served with a lawful request, will Redwood notify us and pause erasure? How will you handle dual obligations (EU data subject requests vs local law enforcement)?

We're attaching our latest annotated redline (Aurum_DPA_Retention_Redlines_v1.docx). Goal is to close retention language with minimal operational work while meeting our compliance team.

Can you propose concrete language and one or two operational options we can present to our InfoSec folks?

Thanks —
Samira
Samira Qureshi
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Aurum HealthTech
Attachments: Aurum_DPA_Retention_Redlines_v1.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira.qureshi@aurumhealth.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Erase-trigger and retention tier questions (DPA redline)

Samira —

Appreciate the clear asks. High level we can offer three pragmatic options (each with operational tradeoffs):

Option A — Strict certified erasure (lowest footprint):
- Customer data and backups deleted within 90 days of request; no onshore cold copies retained beyond 90 days.
- Redwood provides a PDF certification of deletion and a verifiable audit log (S3 object lifecycle + purge events).
- Use case: customers who need demonstrable short TTLs and are comfortable with narrower DR windows.

Option B — Tiered backup window (balanced):
- Primary data erased within 90 days; encrypted cold backups retained for up to 180 days for DR/restore only. Backups are encrypted with keys stored in-region (EU) and accessible only under strict ops procedures.
- Backups flagged as "recover-only" (no live-serving restores except in customer-approved recovery).
- Redwood supplies cryptographic hash manifest and a quarterly backup retention attestation; certified deletion of primary data at 90 days.

Option C — Extended retention w/ legal-hold carve-out (max flexibility):
- 180-day retention for both primary and backup unless a customer-instigated erase triggers a certified deletion workflow; legal holds override retention and are documented.

Operational notes:
- For Option B we can provide an evidence matrix (we'll attach the playbook) and an audit trail that shows key deletion, copy locations, and purge timestamps. Backups in Option B will remain within EU zones; we do not replicate backups to outside jurisdictions without explicit customer consent.

I'll loop in Ops (Priyom) and Sales (Ben) for the technical/contract feasibility and suggested redline text. Which of these three would your security team prefer as a starting point?

Best,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Evidence_Playbook.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Forwarding Aurum's redline and Rishi's options. TL;DR: Aurum needs bounded backup retention and a clear certification of deletion for primary data. They prefer something that doesn't require wholesale onshore copies but need auditable proof.

Ask: can Ops support Option B (90-day primary erase + 180-day encrypted cold backups in-region, recover-only) with the attestation artifacts Rishi referenced? If yes, can you draft a 2-paragraph redline we can send back to Aurum (explicitly call out: EU-only backup storage, KMS key control, and the certification package)?

Attachments: Aurum_DPA_Retention_Redlines_v1.docx (from Samira)

Thanks —
Marissa
VP, Sales Operations

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Erase-trigger and retention tier questions (DPA redline)

Marissa —

We can support Option B with the following constraints and deliverables. Technical confirmation: yes, backups remain in EU regions only, encrypted with a customer-scoped KMS key (or Redwood-managed EU KMS if customer prefers). Backups will be flagged as "recover-only" and access requires a two-person ops approval flow.

Deliverables we can produce for the DPA:
- Quarterly retention attestation (signed) stating backup retention windows and locations.
- Per-erase certified deletion report: timestamped purge events (object IDs), KMS key rotation logs, and a signed statement from Ops.
- Evidence matrix (attached) describing which systems create backups and the expected retention for each.

Suggested redline snippet you can propose to Aurum: 
"Redwood will delete Customer Data from active stores within ninety (90) days of a valid EEA erase request. Redwood may retain encrypted, recover-only backups for up to one hundred eighty (180) days solely for disaster recovery; such backups will be stored only in EU regions and encrypted with keys managed per Section X (KMS controls). Redwood will provide, upon Customer request, a certified deletion report describing purge timestamps, object identifiers, and supporting audit logs. Legal holds will be documented and notified to Customer; Redwood will pause automated erasure for records subject to a documented legal hold."

Attachments: evidence_matrix.csv (contains system-by-system backup retention mapping)

Operational caveats: full destruction of backup media requires coordination across backup/archival vendors and may take an additional 7–14 days after the final purge event to complete physical/immutable artifact lifecycle steps; we will include this timeline in the certification document.

If that language looks good, I'll prep the attestation templates and a short ops playbook for the contract team.

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior Manager, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference
